body:
OBSERVED (2026-08-05). testTargetFor's scripts/ rule is /^scripts\/([^/]+)\.(?:mjs|cjs|js)$/ — the [^/]+ class stops at a slash, so it matches only sources sitting DIRECTLY in scripts/. A source one directory deeper never reaches the same-basename convention even when its test exists and covers it completely.

Live case: scripts/router/check-consolidation.mjs is fully covered by scripts/test/check-consolidation.test.mjs (19 tests), but testTargetFor returns null for it, so classify() puts it on the SLOW path. The slow path runs `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` — the entire 54-segment monorepo suite — ONCE PER MUTANT. Measured: a 2-file diff took >22 minutes and was still running, against ~90 seconds for an equivalent packages/ diff that resolves a fast target. The per-mutant timeout is 600000ms, so the worst case is ~30 minutes for the default 3-mutant slow-path cap.

This is the same slow fallback whose CI environment mismatch is documented in scripts/mutation-gate.mjs's header (v3 note): it needs globally-installed codex/opencode/pi CLIs that the mutation-gate job does not provision, which is why that header says a scripts/ file WITH direct coverage should take the fast single-file path 'instead of ever reaching the slow fallback'. A nested source silently does not, which is a gap in that intent rather than a new idea.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG. Widening the pattern to /^scripts\/(?:.+\/)?([^/]+)\.(?:mjs|cjs|js)$/ makes the live case work and BREAKS a deliberate guard: 'testTargetFor does not match a nested scripts/ path as a top-level script' asserts scripts/sub/mutation-gate.mjs maps to null even though scripts/test/mutation-gate.test.mjs exists. That guard is correct. Those are different files that merely share a basename, and mapping one to the other's test claims coverage that does not exist — the 'coverage gate reports green by not looking' failure this file's own header documents at length. The widened regex was tried, the guard caught it, and it was reverted rather than deleted.

A SAFE FIX must preserve that guard. The mapping may only fire when the basename unambiguously identifies one source. Candidate shapes, in rough order of preference:
(a) Map a nested source only when EXACTLY ONE source file under scripts/** has that basename — scan scripts/ (testTargetFor already takes a `root` parameter, so this stays unit-testable against a fixture tree) and return null on any collision, including collisions between two nested files, not just nested-vs-top-level.
(b) Require the test file to declare the source it covers (a header pragma or a small registry), so the mapping is asserted rather than inferred. More explicit, more ceremony.
(c) A narrow explicit registry of nested source -> test pairs. Simplest and safest, but it has to be maintained by hand and will silently go stale.

Whichever is chosen, absence of a matching test must still map to null and fall through to the slow path: under-claiming coverage is safe, over-claiming is the bug.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
AC1 — the live case resolves: testTargetFor('scripts/router/check-consolidation.mjs') returns 'scripts/test/check-consolidation.test.mjs'. Verify: unit test against a fixture root.
AC2 — the existing guard still holds: with BOTH scripts/mutation-gate.mjs and scripts/sub/mutation-gate.mjs present, the nested one maps to null (it must not claim the top-level file's test). Verify: the existing test 'testTargetFor does not match a nested scripts/ path as a top-level script' passes unchanged, plus a fixture where both files exist.
AC3 — nested-vs-nested collision: two sources in different scripts/ subdirectories sharing a basename both map to null. Verify: fixture test.
AC4 — absent coverage still falls through: a nested source with no same-basename test maps to null. Verify: fixture test.
AC5 — measured improvement: mutation-gate on a diff touching only scripts/router/check-consolidation.mjs selects the fast target and completes in under two minutes. Verify: run it and record the wall clock in the PR.
AC6 — full suite green and mutation-gate clean: npm test; node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12.

PROCESS NOTES. (1) scripts/** is NOT a rails deny-path, so this is not trust-root tier — confirm with the tier classifier rather than assuming. (2) Do not delete the nested-path guard test to make a fix pass; it encodes the false-coverage hazard and any fix must satisfy it as written. (3) Killing a mutation-gate run mid-flight strands a mutant in the working tree — git status before committing.
title: mutation-gate: a source in a scripts/ SUBDIRECTORY cannot reach the same-basename fast target, so it runs the full suite per mutant
